newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary drilling co sets hopes in new Omani owner.
newsitem.headline: Hungary drilling co sets hopes in new Omani owner.

text.p: Hungarian drilling company Koolajkutato Rt said on Monday its new Omani majority owner could provide the company with much-needed foreign contracts.
"The new owner will try to use our excess capacity in the Middle East," Koolajkutato Genereal Manager Ferenc Szecsi told Reuters.
Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt announced last week it had sold an 83 percent stake in Koolajkutato Rt to Oman's MB Petroleum Services Ltd for 4.459 million dollars.
Koolajkutato, a company that provided drilling services to Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt, has been suffering from a reduction in new domestic drillings, Szecsi said.

"Our workforce shrank to 850 from a 3,600 peak in 1986," he said, adding that this was due to the fact that Hungary's oil reserves were well-mapped and domestic demand for the company's services was decreasing steadily.
He added that most of their excess equipment could be suitable for foreign contract jobs after "smaller or larger investments".
At the moment 106 Koolajkutato employees are working on a Syrian project, Szecsi said.
